findings.cross_file_justification: cycle-137 FR-4 adds `cached_keys` (profiles.yaml:31-32) and the `__LOA_PL_ABSENT__` branch (profile-lib.sh:252,256) so the warm path now answers non-profile hot-path knobs straight from .run/effective-config.json and suppresses the live yq read. That widens the authority of a cache file that is read with no provenance check at all.
findings.description: Both cache reads — `_loa_pl_load` (206-209) and the `loa_knob` warm path (247-255) — accept any readable file at `<root>/.run/effective-config.json` whose `schema_version == 1` and `id == $id`. The id (`_loa_pl_id`, 83-89) is `v1|<3 paths>|stat %n|%y|%s` of three files any local reader can stat, so it is forgeable. There is no `[[ ! -L ]]`, no owner-uid check, no group/world-writable check on the file or on `.run`, and `-f` follows a symlink. Contrast `grimoire-index.sh`'s `_gi_trusted_dir` for the decisions cache in the same sprint (grimoire-index.bats 420-448 and the perm/foreign-uid tests), which refuses a symlinked dir or file, a non-uid-owned dir, and an untightenable g/o-writable dir. `_loa_pl_write_cache` itself creates `.run` with `mkdir -p` under the ambient umask (185-186): 775 under umask 002, which the sprint's own comments (grimoire-index.bats 289-290, perf-spawn-budget.bats) say is a real host state. Consequences of a planted or symlinked cache: every `loa_knob` answer for every hook is attacker-chosen (`guardrails.input.enabled`/`guardrails.danger_level.enforce` → false, `known_failures.surface_at_session_start` → true to push KF prose into session context); `forbidden()` runs only in `_loa_pl_build` (130-138), so the warm path serves ANY key including floor keys — `.knobs | has($k)` is the only test; a cached key can be forced to `absent`, hiding an explicit config value; values are printed raw by `jq -r` with no `clean()`, so a consumer that uses the newly cached numeric `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task` inside `(( ))` evaluates attacker arithmetic (`a[$(cmd)]`). A multi-GB planted file also stalls every hook (jq reads the whole file).
findings.failure_mode: A co-tenant with write access to the checkout's `.run/` (group-writable dir created under umask 002, or a shared workspace) writes `effective-config.json` — or a symlink to a file they keep elsewhere and can keep updating — carrying the forged id. From then on the victim's hooks run with the attacker's knob values, the policy floor is bypassed, and the state survives until a config/profiles/floor mtime changes, at which point the attacker re-plants.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the decisions-cache trust boundary to this cache before every read and the write: `.run` and the cache must be owned by `$EUID`; tighten `chmod go-w` when owned, refuse otherwise; require `[[ -f && ! -L ]]` and read via an opened fd (`exec {fd}<`, then `jq ... <&$fd`) to close the TOCTOU; create `.run`/the cache with `umask 077`. Bind the id to a content hash (sha256_portable) of the three inputs rather than mtime+size, as the decisions cache does. Re-apply `forbidden()` to the key on the warm path, or store `profile_keys`+`cached` in the document and refuse keys outside that set. Consider `clean()`-ing served scalar values or validating numeric knobs at the consumer.
findings.failure_scenario: A co-tenant with write access to the checkout's `.run/` (group-writable dir created under umask 002, or a shared workspace) writes `effective-config.json` — or a symlink to a file they keep elsewhere and can keep updating — carrying the forged id. From then on the victim's hooks run with the attacker's knob values, the policy floor is bypassed, and the state survives until a config/profiles/floor mtime changes, at which point the attacker re-plants.

findings.description: The temp file is `$_LOA_PL_CACHE.tmp.$$` — a predictable name — and is written with a plain `>` redirect, which follows an existing symlink (the lib sets no `noclobber`). `mv -f` without `-T` moves the temp INTO a directory if the cache path is a symlink to one. grimoire-index.bats 437-448 explicitly tests the decisions cache against symlinks pre-planted at temp-like names (`AAAAAA XXXXXX 000000 $$ tmp`) and asserts the victim file is untouched; profile-lib has neither the guard nor the test.
findings.failure_mode: A co-tenant who can write `.run/` sprays `effective-config.json.tmp.<pid>` symlinks across a PID range pointing at a victim-writable file (`.loa.config.yaml`, `~/.bashrc`, a chain in `.run/`). The victim's next hook run truncates and overwrites that file with the JSON document; `mv` then installs the symlink itself as the cache, so the clobbered target becomes the cache DISS-001 reads.
findings.suggested_fix: Create the temp with `mktemp` under `umask 077` inside a directory that passed the DISS-001 trust check, verify `[[ ! -L "$tmp" ]]` (or open with `set -o noclobber` so an existing symlink fails), and rename with `mv -f -T`. Add the planted-temp-symlink test from grimoire-index.bats to profile-lib.bats.
findings.failure_scenario: A co-tenant who can write `.run/` sprays `effective-config.json.tmp.<pid>` symlinks across a PID range pointing at a victim-writable file (`.loa.config.yaml`, `~/.bashrc`, a chain in `.run/`). The victim's next hook run truncates and overwrites that file with the JSON document; `mv` then installs the symlink itself as the cache, so the clobbered target becomes the cache DISS-001 reads.

findings.description: The r1/r2 fix makes the memo skip any file whose mtime or ctime is within one second of the clock (stated at 661, 670 and 734). AGC-29 (788-808) and AGC-31 (820-826) write the fixture with `_cfg` and call `agy_opted_in` immediately, with no aging `touch -d`/`_agc_settle` as AGC-27/28/33-36 do, so the memo is never populated and nothing stale can exist. The `stale memo after mv` (796), `stale memo kept for a deleted config` (802), `path switch` (806) and `a forged memo opted in` (825) assertions therefore pass against a lib that drops the inode from the key or that honours `_AGY_NODE_MEMO_KEY/VAL` from the environment. AGC-31 is vacuous a second way: it forges a GNU-shaped key (`%d:%i:%s:%.9Y:%.9Z`) while exporting `_AGY_STAT_STYLE=bsd`, so the lib's computed key (BSD `%d:%i:%z:%m:%c` per `_agc33_shim`, plus the PATH component the lead describes) can never equal the forged one regardless of whether the env is trusted.
findings.failure_mode: A regression that seeds the memo from inherited environment variables — an attacker-set `_AGY_NODE_MEMO_VAL="bool true"` opting the agy route in and putting the prompt on a CLI argv — or that keys on path+size+mtime only (mv replacement served stale) ships green.
findings.suggested_fix: In AGC-29 and AGC-31 age and settle the fixture before the first read (`touch -d "@$(( $(date +%s) - 60 ))"; _agc_settle`), assert `_agc27_calls` proves a hit occurred before each mutation, and in AGC-31 obtain the real key by performing one in-shell hit, reading `_AGY_NODE_MEMO_KEY`, and exporting exactly that pair (same stat style) into the fresh `bash -c` shell.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression that seeds the memo from inherited environment variables — an attacker-set `_AGY_NODE_MEMO_VAL="bool true"` opting the agy route in and putting the prompt on a CLI argv — or that keys on path+size+mtime only (mv replacement served stale) ships green.

findings.description: `_an_audit_chain_summary` and the independent `_oracle` (119-130, missing branch at 125-126) count a chain file that does not exist as valid. LS-1 pins `none → 7/7` (an empty root reports a fully valid audit chain) and `r3-partial → 6/7`, where r3-partial is r3 with the TAMPERED trust-ledger and a valid chain deleted — i.e. deleting a tampered chain raises the score from 5/7 to 6/7. FR-7 deliberately reproduces the per-call count, and the new tests now pin this fail-open semantics in two places, so the `Audit chain: N/7 primitives validate.` cell is not a tamper-evidence signal.
findings.failure_mode: Someone who tampers with `.run/panel-decisions.jsonl` or `grimoires/loa/trust-ledger.jsonl` and sees a red count simply removes the file; loa-status reports a healthy chain and the operator's only in-tool integrity view is silenced.
findings.suggested_fix: Report a third state rather than folding absence into valid: `5 valid / 1 absent / 1 broken` (or count absent as not-valid), and never print `7/7` when any slot is missing. Update LS-1's expectations (`none`, `r3-partial`) and `_oracle` accordingly.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone who tampers with `.run/panel-decisions.jsonl` or `grimoires/loa/trust-ledger.jsonl` and sees a red count simply removes the file; loa-status reports a healthy chain and the operator's only in-tool integrity view is silenced.

findings.description: `forbidden($k)` matches a key equal to a floor glob (`test(globre)`) or an ANCESTOR of a floor key (`split("*")[0] | startswith($k + ".")`), but never a DESCENDANT of a non-glob floor key: with `floor_keys: [a.b]`, the profile or `cached_keys` entry `a.b.c` is allowed. The new `cached_keys` path (135-138) reuses this check, so the gap now also applies to cache-served knobs. Safe only as long as every floor.yaml entry is a leaf scalar or ends in `*`.
findings.failure_mode: A floor entry that names a mapping (e.g. `safety.block_destructive`) can be reached one level below by a profile or cached key, with no WARN.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a descendant clause: `or ($k | startswith(($f | split("*")[0] | rtrimstr(".")) + "."))`, and add a profile-floor.bats case with a mapping-level floor key.
findings.failure_scenario: A floor entry that names a mapping (e.g. `safety.block_destructive`) can be reached one level below by a profile or cached key, with no WARN.

findings.anchor: tests/unit/grimoire-index.bats:decisions cache: a symlinked cache file
findings.description: The decisions-cache trust-boundary suite covers a symlinked dir, a symlinked cache file, pre-planted temp-name symlinks, g/o-writable dirs, a foreign-uid dir, CI env and the opt-out, but no case plants a FIFO or a hard link at `$CACHE`. A reader that `head`s/`awk`s the path (rather than requiring `[[ -f && ! -L ]]` and opening a regular file) blocks on a FIFO forever, hanging the SessionStart hook and loa-status; `_gi_dec_write`'s `cp`/`mktemp` behaviour against a FIFO is likewise unpinned.
findings.failure_mode: A co-tenant who can write `.run/perf-cache/` before the uid-owned dir is tightened runs `mkfifo grimoire-index-decisions.v1.tsv`; every subsequent `grimoire-index.sh` run (and the session start that calls it) blocks indefinitely.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that `mkfifo "$CACHE"` then runs `timeout 10 _gi --tsv`, asserting the cold output, exit 0 and that the FIFO was replaced or ignored; and a hard-link case asserting the linked file is unchanged. Ensure `_gi_dec_read` checks `-f && ! -L` and reads through an fd opened `O_NONBLOCK`-safe (`[[ -p ]]` reject).
findings.failure_scenario: A co-tenant who can write `.run/perf-cache/` before the uid-owned dir is tightened runs `mkfifo grimoire-index-decisions.v1.tsv`; every subsequent `grimoire-index.sh` run (and the session start that calls it) blocks indefinitely.

findings.description: The new perf test runs the production hook under `env -i` (so no `BATS_TEST_FILENAME`/`BATS_VERSION` marker reaches it) with `KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD="$W/ck.sh"`, and asserts the hook consumed the stub's checkpoint (`bd-perf.jsonl` written, 291). That demonstrates a plain environment variable names a script the hook executes (`bash <file> read --json`) in production, ungated. Other seams in this tree are bats-gated (`_kf_test_mode_active`, `LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE`) or WARN once when honoured live (profile-lib.sh 64-66, audit r256-5 / DISS-C-004).
findings.failure_mode: An inherited or leaked variable (a `.envrc`, a CI job, an agent-launched subprocess that re-exports its env) redirects the hook's checkpoint read to an arbitrary script. Same-uid, so a hardening gap rather than a boundary break, but inconsistent with the project's own seam policy.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate `KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD` on a bats marker, or emit the profile-lib-style one-line WARN when it is honoured outside bats; have the perf test pass the marker explicitly rather than relying on `env -i`.
findings.failure_scenario: An inherited or leaked variable (a `.envrc`, a CI job, an agent-launched subprocess that re-exports its env) redirects the hook's checkpoint read to an arbitrary script. Same-uid, so a hardening gap rather than a boundary break, but inconsistent with the project's own seam policy.

findings.description: `CMP_STUB_HOLD_S=240` (107) and the CMP-55 override `CMP_STUB_HOLD_S=300` (1682) are plain shell assignments, not exported, while the stub branches (186, 210, 236) expand `${CMP_STUB_HOLD_S:-300}` at run time. If the stub executes in a child process (a cheval shim on PATH or an `export -f`'d function), the variable is unset there and every reaped hold stays at 300 s — the pre-change behaviour — so the Task 2.5 shortening and CMP-55's negative control are no-ops. Only matters if the stub is not a function invoked in the test shell itself; confirm and export if so.
findings.failure_mode: Orphaned stub holds linger 300 s instead of 240 s after a reaper regression; no security impact, but the FR-6 change silently does nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: `export CMP_STUB_HOLD_S=240` in setup() and `export CMP_STUB_HOLD_S=300` in CMP-55, or assert inside one stub branch that the value it saw equals the test's expectation.
findings.failure_scenario: Orphaned stub holds linger 300 s instead of 240 s after a reaper regression; no security impact, but the FR-6 change silently does nothing.
